fixes.title: Fix Toronto local visibility signals (name + captions + geotags)
fixes.whyItMatters: Discovery is currently constrained by weak, inconsistent location/category signals; adding clear Toronto + category cues helps people in the 6ix find BoxBuddy when searching and browsing locally.
fixes.exactAction: Update your Instagram name field and captions to include: "Toronto moving app" or "moving & home inventory app in Toronto". Add a Toronto geotag to every post for the next 30 days (use a consistent one, e.g., a Toronto landmark or 'Toronto, ON'). Also include one explicit Toronto keyword in the first line of each caption (e.g., 'Moving in Toronto?').
fixes.evidence: Local visibility score is 21/100, and the only location signals noted are 'toronto, the 6ix, the 6, the six'.

fixes.title: Create and pin a link path to get installs (A/B test link-in-bio + pinned posts)
fixes.whyItMatters: Profile conversion is 55/100; visitors likely decide quickly. A clear, tested install pathway (optimized link target + pinned proof posts) increases the chance they follow through.
fixes.exactAction: Do an A/B test for 14 days: change the link-in-bio URL target between (A) the main https://boxbuddy.tech/links and (B) a more direct install landing page if available on that domain. Then pin TWO posts: Pin 1 = 'Track every box' demo, Pin 2 = 'Home inventory made easy' checklist. Keep both pinned descriptions under 2 lines and end each with: 'Download BoxBuddy from the link in bio.'
fixes.evidence: Profile conversion score is 55/100, and the next move listed is 'A/B test the link-in-bio destination and pinned posts.'

fixes.title: Build a signature content format that drives saves/shares (and stop posting the rest)
fixes.whyItMatters: Content performance score is 60/100 but the data says '0.00% across 0 posts', indicating tracking gaps or insufficient reliable measurement. A repeatable, high-save format will create measurable engagement and improve reach via shares.
fixes.exactAction: Switch your next 3 posts to one repeatable format called: 'Toronto Move Checklist (BoxBuddy)' carousel. Slide-by-slide: (1) hook: 'Moving in Toronto? Save this box checklist', (2) materials list, (3) room-by-room labeling plan, (4) inventory photo template, (5) how to track boxes in BoxBuddy, (6) closing: 'Download BoxBuddy from the link in bio.' After you post the 3, keep only posts that are clearly carousel-based for the next 14 days; pause or rewrite any non-checklist formats to fit this structure.
fixes.evidence: Content performance score is 60/100 and the dataset shows '0.00% across 0 posts'; the category context suggests checklists/carousels are save/share magnets, and the competitor-gap note implies you need a differentiating signature format.

fixes.title: Add one explicit app install CTA to every post (aligned to 'app' kind)
fixes.whyItMatters: Sales readiness is 37/50; attention without a clear next step reduces conversion. As an app, your CTAs must point to download/try/link-in-bio.
fixes.exactAction: Edit the caption (and, if you use it, the first pinned comment) on every upcoming post so the last line is exactly: 'Download BoxBuddy from the link in bio to track every box.' If you do Stories: add a story slide with the same line and include a swipe-up only if you have it; otherwise point to link-in-bio.
fixes.evidence: Sales readiness is 37/50 and the next move listed is 'Add one explicit CTA to every post and a clear link path.'

fixes.title: Differentiate with a signature 'Box Labels + Inventory' system competitors don’t use
fixes.whyItMatters: Competitor gap is strong (90/100), but you still need visible differentiation. A consistent system (label templates + inventory workflow) makes BoxBuddy instantly recognizable versus generic moving planners.
fixes.exactAction: Create 3 assets in one batch: (1) a printable/visual 'Room + Box Number' label example, (2) a 'Photo inventory template' (what to photograph + how to name), (3) a short workflow graphic: 'Label → Scan/track → Find room quickly'. Post as a carousel under the same hook: 'Your BoxBuddy Label System (Toronto Edition)'. End each carousel with: 'Try BoxBuddy from the link in bio.'
fixes.evidence: Competitor gap score is 90/100 and suggests you can differentiate; the listed next move is 'Differentiate with a signature format competitors don't use.'

hookFormulas: Stop losing track of boxes during your move in {city}: here’s the quick system

The easiest way to inventory your home: {simple action} → {result}
Moving day chaos vs. your plan: use {appName} to {outcome}
Before you move: {number} minutes to make unpacking easier
Your boxes have a story—turn it into an inventory you can find in seconds
What to label your boxes (Toronto move edition) — no guessing
Packing hacks for small spaces in Toronto: inventory first, pack second
New place, same mess? Try the box tracking workflow that prevents it
captionFormulas:
Hook (1 line) → Problem (1–2 lines) → Simple system (3–5 lines) → Toronto-specific example (1 line) → Benefit (1 line) → How to get started (1 line with link-in-bio/download language).

Example: “Toronto move? Don’t ‘hope you’ll remember.’ Build your box inventory while packing. Here’s the workflow: (1) Create rooms, (2) Scan/track boxes, (3) Note priority items, (4) Keep a quick unpack plan. Imagine labeling boxes for your Yonge/Eglinton move or a condo storage locker—then finding everything when you need it.”

Mini-story: “We’ve all done this…” → What went wrong → The fix → Result → CTA (download/try via link in bio).

Template: “We’ve all done this… but it costs time on moving day. The fix is simple: track each box as you pack. Your future self will thank you when you’re searching for essentials.”

Pain → Promise → Steps → Proof prompt (ask a question) → CTA.

Template: “Tired of opening the wrong box? Promise: you’ll know what’s inside before you unpack. Steps: 1) assign boxes to rooms, 2) track them, 3) set an unpack order. Question: what’s the one box you never want to lose? Try BoxBuddy via the link in bio.”

Myth vs. Reality: “Myth: labeling is enough. Reality: inventory is what saves you time.” → What to do instead → CTA.

Template: “Labeling helps, but inventory + tracking is what makes your move predictable. Build your box list as you pack—then keep it for storage and future moves. Get the app via the link in bio.”

Feature-to-outcome mapping (non-technical): “Create plan → Track boxes → Simplify unpacking.” Include a Toronto context line (condo, stairs, storage locker, small-space packing).

Template: “Create your moving & home inventory plan, track every box, and simplify unpacking—especially helpful in Toronto condos where storage space is tight. Try BoxBuddy via link in bio.”
ctaOptions: Try BoxBuddy on your next move — link in bio
Download BoxBuddy 📦 — start tracking your boxes today (link in bio)
Use BoxBuddy to build your home inventory — link in bio
Get started in minutes — BoxBuddy is ready via the link in bio
Simplify unpacking before it happens — download BoxBuddy (link in bio)
reelIdeas: “Toronto Move in Real Time” — show packing a single room while updating a box inventory (fast cuts: label → track → quick room list). End with “find essentials faster” message + CTA via link in bio.

“What to label your boxes (Toronto condo edition)” — reel shows sample labels/box numbering system on-screen; voiceover: what goes on label + why inventory helps when you’re juggling elevators/stairs.
“Stop unpacking blindly” — show opening three “random” boxes in a mock scenario, then reveal how an inventory prevents the wasted minutes (inventory screenshot-style).
“Storage locker clarity” — show how to track boxes you’ll keep in storage (inventory view) so you don’t forget what’s where later.
“5-minute pre-move setup” — quick walkthrough: create rooms, plan essentials priority, then start tracking boxes as you pack.
“Unpacking order” — demonstrate setting an unpack priority (essentials first), then show the inventory list guiding you room by room.
carouselIdeas:
Carousel: “Toronto Moving Checklist: inventory-first method”
Slides: (1) Title: Inventory-first = faster unpacking (Toronto) (2) Create room list (3) Decide essentials priority (4) Track each box as you pack (5) Keep inventory notes for storage (6) Unpack in your planned order (7) CTA slide: “Download BoxBuddy via link in bio.”

Carousel: “Box Labeling System (that actually works)”
Slides: (1) Why ‘misc’ fails (2) Room codes example (3) Box number rules (4) Priority tags (5) What to record inside notes (6) How inventory ties it together (7) CTA slide.

Carousel: “Home Inventory for Toronto Households”
Slides: (1) Why home inventory helps beyond moving (2) What to include (3) Room-by-room approach (4) Storage / seasonal items (5) Search/find mindset (6) Build it gradually (7) CTA slide with link in bio.

Carousel: “Packing without regret: a single-room workflow”
Slides: (1) Pick one room (2) Create that room in your inventory (3) Track each box (4) Add a quick contents note (5) Set unpack order (6) Finish with a simple ‘essentials’ list (7) CTA slide.

Carousel: “Before you move: the 3 things to do today”
Slides: (1) Don’t wait—plan rooms (2) Start inventory early (3) Assign priority items (4) Track storage boxes (5) Screenshot/keep your inventory list (6) Unpack faster (7) CTA slide.
proofIdeas: Process proof (no stats): “Before/After workflow” carousel: Before = unlabeled boxes + guessing; After = tracked boxes by room with an unpack order.
User-intent proof: “Essentials test” reel where you show finding essentials in the inventory list before opening boxes (visual proof of reduced searching).
Consistency proof: “Week of moving” carousel sequence: Room 1 inventory complete → Room 2 → Room 3; show the list growing and making unpacking easier.
Storage proof: “What’s in this box?” scenario for items kept in storage; show how inventory notes prevent forgetting.
Clarity proof: “One-room example” graphic: a single room inventory list with box names/contents and how it maps to unpacking order.
